I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. For me, that is the safest way to use the full year, match local weather and irrigation habits, and protect household income. At the start of the growing season, my wheat is already in the field, so I will manage it carefully through spring with topdressing, one to two irrigations depending on soil moisture, and disease control only when pressure is visible. After wheat harvest, I will quickly prepare the land and plant summer maize with improved seed, because maize fits well after wheat, uses the summer heat and rain, and gives me stable yield. I will not spread myself across too many crops this year. I would rather do two familiar crops well than take more risk with something less steady. I will use moderate fertilizer, watch water closely, and keep pesticide use limited to what I think the field actually needs.
